external_entities.name: shopper
external_entities.description: A person who browses the storefront, signs in, and places orders.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Shoppers sign in with email and password and get a session cookie

external_entities.name: card processor
external_entities.description: A third-party payment processor that settles payments and sends payment webhooks.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our card processor is a third party.

processes.name: storefront API
processes.description: A Node service running on Cloud Run that serves the storefront, accepts orders, and receives payment webhooks.
processes.source_excerpt: the storefront API, a Node service running on Cloud Run
processes.technology: Node service running on Cloud Run

processes.name: order service
processes.description: A Python worker in the core network that processes orders, accesses the orders database, and writes receipts.
processes.source_excerpt: The order service is a Python worker in our core network

data_stores.name: orders-db
data_stores.description: A PostgreSQL database containing orders, shopper addresses, and card-last-four.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Orders, shopper addresses and card-last-four live in a PostgreSQL database (orders-db)

data_stores.name: receipt archive
data_stores.description: A Cloud Storage bucket containing completed-order receipts.
data_stores.source_excerpt: a Cloud Storage bucket we call the receipt archive

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.source_excerpt: Shoppers sign in with email and password and get a session cookie

data_flows.name: place orders
data_flows.source_excerpt: place orders through the storefront API
data_flows.notes: MFA has not been rolled out for shopper accounts.

data_flows.name: submit order
data_flows.source_excerpt: the storefront API calls the order service over gRPC

data_flows.name: read and write
data_flows.source_excerpt: the order service reads and writes with a single application account that has full read/write
data_flows.notes: The application account password comes from an environment variable on the worker.

data_flows.name: write receipt
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every completed order also gets a receipt written to a Cloud Storage bucket
data_flows.data_description: receipt recording which order was written and that the order service wrote it

data_flows.name: payment webhook
data_flows.source_excerpt: After they settle a payment they POST a webhook back to the storefront API to tell us the order is paid.
data_flows.notes: The source says: "I would have to check how that callback is authenticated."
data_flows.data_description: payment settlement notification that the order is paid

trust_boundaries.name: core network
trust_boundaries.description: The network in which the order service runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The order service is a Python worker in our core network

trust_boundaries.name: card processor
trust_boundaries.description: The separate control zone of the third-party card processor.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Our card processor is a third party.

assumptions.assumption: The orders database contains confidential data because it stores shopper addresses and card-last-four alongside orders.
assumptions.basis: The source states that orders-db stores shopper addresses and card-last-four.

assumptions.assumption: The receipt archive contains confidential data because it stores completed-order receipts.
assumptions.basis: The source states that every completed order gets a receipt written to the receipt archive.

assumptions.assumption: The order service presents a non-web interface because it is a worker reached through gRPC rather than a web application interface.
assumptions.basis: The source describes the component as a Python worker and says the storefront API calls it over gRPC.

assumptions.assumption: The card processor occupies a tenant boundary because it is controlled by a third party.
assumptions.basis: The source explicitly states that the card processor is a third party.
